hero.headline: Turn your entrepreneurship programme into a measurable result
hero.problem: Programmes run on spreadsheets, email and paper judging forms — and nobody can measure what was actually learned.
hero.solution: BizSim brings training, exams, business simulations, hackathons and certificates into one platform. Every participant's progress is recorded automatically, and every jury score stays transparent per criterion.
hero.reassurance: No installation · Under your own brand · AZ / TR / EN
hero.screenshot: Tenant admin dashboard: active programmes, participant counts and the weekly progress chart

proof.title: Who it is built for
proof.quote: “Collecting the results of one hackathon used to take two weeks. Now jury scores appear per criterion immediately, and participants get their feedback the same day.”
proof.attribution: Programme director · sample text, to be replaced with a real customer quote

features.title: Every stage of the programme in one place
features.description: From registration to certificate, without stitching separate tools together.

a.title: Video training and exams
a.body: Lessons play as a playlist and each completion is recorded separately. Exams are graded on the server — correct answers never reach the browser.
a.screenshot: Participant training screen: video player, lesson playlist and progress bar

b.title: Business simulation
b.body: Participants decide round by round while cash, customer satisfaction and reputation move in real time. Scenarios are pure data, so a new one needs no code.
b.screenshot: Simulation play screen: round context, decision options and the metric gauges

c.title: Hackathon and judging
c.body: Teams form, submit a project PDF, and jurors score and comment against each criterion. Results stay sealed until you reveal them, then each team sees anonymous feedback.
c.screenshot: Jury scoring screen: PDF preview and per-criterion score sliders

d.title: Certificates and analytics
d.body: Certificates are issued as PDFs with a serial number and a verification code. The analytics dashboard shows completion per course, average scores and weekly activity.
d.screenshot: Analytics dashboard: KPI cards, the weekly activity chart and the course table

steps.title: How it works
steps.description: Once your account is open you run the programme yourself — we never touch your content.

one.title: Receive your account
one.body: We open an account with your seat limit and email the admin credentials. Two-factor authentication is set up on first sign-in.

two.title: Set up your programme
two.body: Pick the training, simulation and hackathon modules you need, define the judging criteria, and invite participants by QR code or invite link.

three.title: Measure the results
three.body: Who finished what, what the average score is, which team scored what on which criterion — it all lands in the dashboard and exports to CSV.

pricingPreview.title: Build your programme from services
pricingPreview.description: Pick the modules you need — pricing is per participant and drops as numbers grow. No hidden fees.

cta.title: See the platform on your own scenario
cta.body: Let us show you how your programme would be set up, in a 15-minute demo. We reply within one business day.

features.title: Six modules, one platform
features.description: Each module can be switched on or off, so you do not pay for what your organisation does not use.

trainings.title: Video training with lesson tracking
trainings.body: A training is a playlist of lessons, and every completion is recorded on its own. Progress is therefore computed from real events rather than estimated. Content is stored in three languages and shown in the participant's own.
trainings.screenshot: Training detail: video player, lesson playlist on the right, progress bar below

exams.title: Exams graded on the server
exams.body: Questions are served one at a time and answers are checked on the server — the correct answers never reach the browser, so a result cannot be tampered with from the client. The result screen shows the given answer, the correct one and an explanation for every question.
exams.screenshot: Exam result screen: score, pass state and the per-question explanation list

simulations.title: Data-driven business simulation
simulations.body: Participants decide round by round, and each choice moves cash, customer satisfaction and reputation. A small amount of market noise is applied, so the same strategy does not produce an identical run twice. A teacher can also grade the run by hand.

bullets.a: A new scenario needs no code

simulations.screenshot: Scenario editor: rounds, choices and the metric effects of each choice

hackathon.title: Hackathons with transparent judging
hackathon.body: Participants form teams and upload a project PDF; jurors score and comment against each criterion. Rankings use a weighted average, so who scored what on which criterion stays auditable afterwards. Results stay sealed until you reveal them.
hackathon.screenshot: Live ranking table: teams, weighted score and the per-criterion breakdown

certificates.title: Verifiable certificates
certificates.body: Participation, achievement and completion certificates are issued as PDFs. Each carries a per-organisation sequential serial and a random verification code, and is frozen with the name and title held at issue time — renaming someone later does not alter the document.
certificates.screenshot: Certificate template preview: serial number, signature fields and verification code

analytics.title: See the state of the programme in numbers
analytics.body: The analytics dashboard shows total and active participants, enrolments, average completion and certificates issued. The course table carries enrolled, completed, average score and average duration, and the weekly chart tracks the last twelve weeks.

bullets.a: Completion and average score per course

analytics.screenshot: Analytics dashboard: KPI cards, the weekly activity line and the sortable course table

a.question: What is a seat and how is it counted?
a.answer: One seat is one participant with an account. A seat is taken at registration and released when the participant is removed. Admin, teacher and jury accounts do not consume seats.

b.question: How does billing work?
b.answer: Subscriptions are monthly and billed on the seat count. You can pay by card online, or by invoiced bank transfer for institutions.

c.question: Can I change plan mid-term?
c.answer: Yes. You can raise your plan or seat count at any time and the difference is prorated for the current period. Reductions take effect from the next period.

d.question: Where is our data stored?
d.answer: Each organisation's data is isolated and enforced at the database level. Certificates and project files are held in encrypted object storage. Details are in the privacy policy.

e.question: Do you provide a contract and invoices?
e.answer: Yes. We sign a written contract with institutions and issue an invoice for each period. We also provide the documents procurement and tender processes require.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.draftNotice: DRAFT — this text has not been through legal review and is not binding.

controller.heading: Data controller
controller.body: The organisation using the platform is the controller for its participants' data and BizSim is the processor. For data sent to us directly through the marketing site, BizSim is the controller.

dataCollected.heading: Data we collect
dataCollected.body:
Account details (name, email, phone, role), academic profile (university, faculty, specialty, year), usage events (lesson completions, exam attempts, sign-in records) and uploaded files (project PDFs, avatars).

Through the demo form: name, company, email, phone, estimated participant count and message.

purposes.heading: Purposes
purposes.body: Delivering the service, tracking participant progress, issuing and verifying certificates, investigating security incidents, billing and support.

legalBasis.heading: Legal basis
legalBasis.body: Performance of a contract (delivering the service), legitimate interest (security and abuse prevention), legal obligation (accounting) and consent (the marketing form).

sharing.heading: Sharing with third parties
sharing.body: We do not sell data. It is shared only with the processors the service needs: cloud infrastructure, email delivery and the payment provider. A data processing agreement is in place with each.

transfers.heading: International transfers
transfers.body: Processing takes place primarily on servers in the European region. Where a transfer outside that region occurs, legal mechanisms such as standard contractual clauses apply.

retention.heading: Retention
retention.body: Account data is kept for the life of the subscription and for as long as the law requires afterwards. Issued certificates are kept longer so they remain verifiable. Demo form submissions are deleted once the sales process ends.

security.heading: Security measures
security.body: Encrypted connections, hashed passwords, mandatory two-factor authentication for admin roles, role-based authorisation, organisation isolation enforced at the database level, and an audit log.

rights.heading: Your rights
rights.body:
You have the right to access, rectify, erase, restrict, port and object to the processing of your data. See the contact section below to make a request.

Note: for data held by an organisation you participate in, address the request to that organisation first.

cookies.heading: Cookies
cookies.body: Only cookies the service needs are used: session, language preference and interface theme. No advertising or tracking cookies are set.

changes.heading: Changes to this policy
changes.body: When this document is updated the date above changes. Significant changes are announced to organisation admins by email.

contact.heading: Contact
contact.body: For privacy questions and data requests, use the form on the contact page and mention “Privacy” in your message.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.draftNotice: DRAFT — this text has not been through legal review and is not binding.

acceptance.heading: Acceptance
acceptance.body: By using the platform you accept these terms. Where a separate agreement has been signed on behalf of an organisation, that agreement prevails in case of conflict.

service.heading: The service
service.body: BizSim is a multi-tenant software service covering training, exams, simulations, hackathons, certificates and analytics. Which modules are active depends on the subscription plan.

accounts.heading: Accounts and security
accounts.body: Users are responsible for the security of their account. Two-factor authentication is mandatory for admin roles. Sharing credentials is prohibited.

seats.heading: Seat licensing
seats.body: A subscription is capped by its seat count. When the cap is reached no further participant can register. The seat count can be raised at any time.

acceptableUse.heading: Acceptable use
acceptableUse.body: The platform may not be used for unlawful purposes, to infringe the rights of others, to attempt unauthorised access, or for automated bulk requests.

content.heading: Content and ownership
content.body: Content an organisation uploads (programmes, scenarios, projects) belongs to that organisation. The platform itself, its code and its design belong to BizSim.

availability.heading: Availability
availability.body: We aim for uninterrupted service, but planned maintenance and provider-side outages can occur. Planned work is announced in advance.

fees.heading: Fees
fees.body: Fees are billed monthly on the seat count. Service may be suspended if payment is late. Price changes are announced at least one billing period in advance.

termination.heading: Termination
termination.body: A subscription can be cancelled at the end of the current period. Serious breach of these terms may lead to immediate suspension. A reasonable window for data export is given after cancellation.

liability.heading: Limitation of liability
liability.body: To the extent permitted by law, we are not liable for indirect damages. Total liability is limited to the subscription fees paid in the preceding twelve months.

governingLaw.heading: Governing law
governingLaw.body: These terms are governed by the law of the country in which the provider is registered. Disputes are heard by the competent courts of that jurisdiction.

contact.heading: Contact
contact.body: For questions about these terms, use the form on the contact page.
